Predicates:
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided financial aid.
Hardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.

Applicant(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE.
LiveInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to y.
TestCost(y) ::: y is the cost of taking a test.
CheaperThan(y, z) ::: y costs less than z.
ProvidesFinancialAid(y, x) ::: y provides financial aid to x.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
Family(x) ::: x is a family member.
Employed(x) ::: x is employed.
ResourcesAvailable(x) ::: x has resources available.
LivingInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
ApplyingToGRE(x) ::: x applies to take the GRE.
Test(y) ::: y is a test.
Cost(y) ::: y is the cost of a test.
Question: Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.

Conclusion: ¬∃x (Applying(x, GRE) ∧ ∃y (ProvidesFinancialAid(y, x))) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
